small_guidance:
- The current fused conv+softmax+pool kernel extracts per-(kd,kh,kw) weight slices via a masked sum over a KVOL axis — this wastes work. Preload weights as `[OC, IC_C, KD, KH, KW]` directly indexed by static loop vars (`w_all[:, :, kd, kh, kw]` via separate loads or reshape) so each inner iteration is a clean `tl.sum(w*x)` without the mask trick.
- Add an autotune over `IC_C` rounding and try `num_warps=1` since OC=16 is tiny (one warp can hold the [OC] vector); also try `num_stages=4` to overlap the 64 inner conv loads.
- Pull the input loads out of the (kd,kh,kw) inner triple: for each (od,oh,ow), load a `[IC_C, KD, KH, KW]` window once, then the conv reduces to a single `tl.sum(w_all * x_window)` over all axes — eliminates 27× redundant loads per pool position.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per `(N, output-spatial tile of pre-pool grid)` computing `[OC, TILE]` via `tl.dot` over `IC*KD*KH*KW`. Since OC=16, pad K-tile to a dot-friendly shape (e.g. BLOCK_N=32 spatial, BLOCK_K=32) and let `tl.dot` do the heavy lifting instead of scalar `tl.sum` accumulations.
- Separate the pipeline into two kernels: (1) a conv-GEMM producing the full `(N,16,14,30,30)` conv output (or per-tile), (2) a softmax+double-pool kernel that does channel softmax then 4×4×4 max-reduction in one pass over the channel-contiguous tile. Trying to fuse conv into the pool loop forces 8× redundant conv compute per pool window.
- Use NHWDC (channels-last) layout for the conv output so the 16-channel softmax reduction is a contiguous vector load; this also lets the pool kernel coalesce its 64-element spatial window per channel tile.
